objective.text: Treat VITE-prefixed environment values as client-visible rather than server secrets.

difficulty.rationale: Keep a server credential out of data deliberately bundled into browser code.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: Vite uses its default environment prefix. Client code references import.meta.env.VITE_PAYMENT_SECRET.

stem: A developer places a server payment credential in VITE_PAYMENT_SECRET, expecting .env to stay private. What is the correct review finding?

options.text: The referenced value can be bundled into client code; keep this credential server-side.
options.rationale: The VITE_ prefix opts a value into client exposure. A private source .env file does not make the resulting browser bundle secret.

options.text: Production minification encrypts the value against browser users.
options.rationale: Minification is not confidentiality protection for data delivered to the client.
options.misconception: Minification is not confidentiality protection for data delivered to the client.

options.text: The value remains private because .env itself is not served by Laravel.
options.rationale: Build-time substitution can expose the value without serving the original file.
options.misconception: Build-time substitution can expose the value without serving the original file.

options.text: Calling config:cache removes the value from an already generated JavaScript bundle.
options.rationale: Laravel’s configuration cache does not rewrite a built client artifact.
options.misconception: Laravel’s configuration cache does not rewrite a built client artifact.

contains: Variables prefixed with VITE_ will be exposed in client-side source code after Vite bundling.
validation.reason: Official Vite environment contract, default prefix and a referenced value. No Vite bundler execution is claimed.
